{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A is a purely digital product. The brief cites working agentic research pipelines from small teams (Foray, Gixo), so one person with AI agents can plausibly build and deliver it within 90 days. Idea B's own case against says its hard parts are sourcing, warehousing, customs, breakage and address failures, which are physical-logistics problems that agents do not solve.",
    "A cites five competitors, four with sourced public prices from $10/mo to $299/mo, plus a $60 per-blueprint option. That shows self-serve willingness to pay at price points a solo founder can sell into. B's price evidence points to enterprise terms (Sendoso at $15k-$20k+/yr) and to self-serve tiers that require ongoing per-kit spend of $30-$75 on top of the subscription.",
    "B's case for rests on wiring Stripe webhooks to an 'existing swag-fulfillment API'. The brief names no such API and cites no source for one, so its feasibility claim is unsupported. A's feasibility claim cites named, comparable builds.",
    "Both niches are crowded, so saturation does not separate them. A's direct channel to a first sale is also clearer: the pain is voiced natively on Indie Hackers and LinkedIn, where a founder can reach operators personally. B depends on passing Stripe app review or on paid social at a cited $150-$250 per MQL/SQL."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's only quoted demand signal is a LinkedIn commenter asking which vendor Stripe used to send gifts. That person was receiving a gift, not buying a tool, and the brief admits as much. The 'seed HN quote' it mentions is never reproduced, so it counts as missing. B therefore has no shown evidence of a small-SaaS buyer who wants to pay for this.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A's demand evidence is also thin: two pain quotes and no purchase intent. One quote ('Only you can') arguably argues against a tool choosing for the user. A's paid acquisition (~$104 cost per lead) is poor against a $60 one-off price, and its organic channels are unquantified. A wins mainly because B carries extra physical-fulfillment risk and an enterprise-shaped market, not because A's demand is proven."
}
